children: Anant Ambani says the investment will fund compressed biogas plants in the state, with the projects expected to generate nearly Rs 60,000 crore in revenue over the coming decades

Reliance Industries plans to invest Rs 1 lakh crore in Andhra Pradesh to establish compressed biogas (CBG) plants, with the projects expected to create more than 3 lakh jobs and generate nearly Rs 60,000 crore in revenue for the state over the coming decades.

Announcing the investment on Friday, October 2, Reliance Industries Executive Director Anant M Ambani said the initiative would support India's clean energy transition while creating new economic opportunities for farmers and rural communities.

Speaking at the foundation stone-laying ceremony for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub and the Indian School of Agriculture (ISA) in Madanapalle, Ambani said the investment would help farmers contribute to the country's energy security alongside their role in food production.
"Our kisans, who ensure India's food security, will now strengthen India's energy security too — making India self-reliant in energy," he said.

The proposed CBG plants will convert agricultural residue, animal dung, food waste and other biomass into methane-rich gas, providing an alternative to conventional natural gas. The projects are expected to create new avenues for agricultural waste utilisation, rural employment and renewable energy production.
Reliance To Expand Clean Energy Footprint In Rayalaseema

The proposed investment is part of Reliance's broader clean energy push in Andhra Pradesh, with the company also exploring opportunities in advanced manufacturing and investing in clean energy projects in the Rayalaseema region.

Ambani said the state had approved 388 mega projects since June 2024, involving investment commitments exceeding Rs 14 lakh crore and the potential to generate nearly 11 lakh jobs. Around a third of these investments are expected to be directed towards Rayalaseema, citing state government data.

The announcement builds on Reliance's earlier plans to establish compressed biogas facilities in Andhra Pradesh. In April 2025, the company announced an investment of Rs 65,000 crore to develop 500 CBG plants across the state. The latest Rs 1 lakh crore announcement signals a larger proposed investment, although the precise relationship between the two plans and their implementation timelines has not been detailed.
Reliance To Support Technology-Led Agriculture
Beyond energy, Reliance will support the Indian School of Agriculture through strategic investment, digital capabilities, technical expertise and industry partnerships.

The proposed institution aims to combine artificial intelligence (AI) and modern agricultural technologies with traditional farming knowledge. Its focus areas will include pest prediction, drone-based crop monitoring, precision irrigation, robotics and price intelligence.

Ambani said Jio would collaborate with the institution to deliver farmer training programmes in Indian languages through virtual classrooms in villages. The initiative will also seek to train rural youth as digitally enabled agricultural extension workers.

The school is expected to support the broader objectives of the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub, which is designed to promote technology-driven agriculture and strengthen agricultural value chains in the region.

The horticulture hub has a proposed outlay of Rs 40,000 crore, according to Ambani's remarks at the event. Separately, the broader government-backed project has been reported as a Rs 1 lakh crore initiative, comprising Rs 40,000 crore in central assistance and Rs 60,000 crore in private investment. Its objectives include expanding horticulture cultivation, improving processing and marketing infrastructure, and strengthening export capabilities in Rayalaseema.
The Times of India

"Today, we are not just laying foundation stones. We are laying the foundations for rural enterprise, stronger villages, a more sustainable India, and most importantly, for improving the lives of our farmers," Ambani said.

The investment announcement comes as Andhra Pradesh seeks to attract large-scale industrial investment while expanding its renewable energy capacity and modernising agriculture. For Reliance, the proposed CBG expansion also creates an opportunity to link agricultural waste management with clean energy production and rural economic activity.
The scale of the proposed investment, however, will ultimately be measured by project execution, capital deployment and the extent to which the projected employment and revenue benefits materialise.
